THIS MISCELLANEOUS FIRST APPEAL IS FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF MV ACT PRAYING TO MODIFY THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 05.03.2015 PASSED IN MVC NO.4321/2012 ON THE FILE OF THE XXI ADDITIONAL CHIEF METROPOLITAN MAGISTRATE AND XXIII ADDITIONAL SMALL CAUSES JUDGE, MACT, COURT OF SMALL CAUSES, BENGALURU,
PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.
 THIS MISCELLANEOUS FIRST APPEAL COMING ON FOR FURTHER HEARING THIS DAY, K.S.MUDAGAL J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT Heard.
2. "Whether the compensation awarded to the appellant under the impugned award is just"? is the question involved in this case.
3. The appellant is a software engineer working with HP Software.
On 02.01.2012 at 8.30 a.m. when the appellant was traveling in a private bus bearing Registration No.KA-21-8559 the said bus met with the accident near Marur Head Post, Mangalore-Bangalore Highway.
In the accident, she suffered D6 stable burst fracture with 50% decrease in height.
She also suffered D5 and D8 Superior and plate compression fracture.
Initially she was treated in Government Hospital, Nelamangala.
From there she was shifted to Fortis Hospital.
She was treated as inpatient from 02.01.2012 to 08.01.2012.
PW.2 who examined her deposed that she was suffering from Khyphosis deformity of D6 region leading to her back pain and she suffered 20% permanent physical disability to her whole body.

4. The appellant filed M.V.C.No.4321/2012 before MACT and Small Causes Court, Bangalore (SCCH-25) against the respondents claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- and contended that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the bus by its driver.

entities.text: MACT and Small Causes Court, Bangalore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Due to the accident,
she has suffered loss of future earnings due to permanent physical disability suffered by her.

She also claimed compensation on the head of loss of income during laid up period, medical expenses,
attendant charges and amenities etc.
5. Respondent No.1 did not contest the petition.

Respondent No.2 alone contested the petition denying occurrence of the accident, rashness and negligence on the part of the driver of the bus,
injuries suffered by the appellant, age, occupation, income and its liability to pay the compensation.

Priyadarshini G.K vs Sathish on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83650990/
2 6.
The Tribunal on recording the evidence and hearing the parties, by the impugned award held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the bus by its driver.

Though the Tribunal accepted the evidence of PW.2 with regard to disability, it held that since the appellant continued in service, got promotion and was earning more than what she was earning at the time of the accident,
there was no loss of earnings.

However, the Tribunal awarded total compensation on other heads as follows:
 Sl. Particulars Compensation  No. awarded in Rs.
 1 Pain and suffering 30,000/-
 2 Loss of income during 61,600/-
 laid up period  3 Medical expenses 86,766/-
 4 Attendant Charges 10,000/-
 5 Loss of beauty amenities 25,000/-
 & happiness

7. The appellant challenges the said award on the ground that the Tribunal ought to have awarded loss of future earnings and the compensation awarded on other heads is also on the lower side.
8.
Reiterating the grounds of the appeal, Sri P.N.Varadaraj, learned Counsel for the appellant seeks enhancement of the compensation amount.
9. Per contra, Sri B.C.Shivanne Gowda, learned Counsel for the Insurer justifies the impugned award.
He submits that the appellant continued in service.
Therefore there is no loss of future earnings.

10. Though appellant's Counsel contended that after the accident, the appellant could not continue the job and she has resigned her employment, no material is placed to substantiate the said contention.
As against that the appellant herself in her evidence has admitted that after she was promoted, her salary was enhanced from Rs.3,00,000/- to Rs.3,90,000/-.

Under the circumstances,
the Tribunal was justified in not awarding compensation on the head of loss of future earnings.
11. So far as the compensation on the head of pain and sufferings, there were three fractures with compression.
The doctor's evidence shows that the appellant had deformity of D6 region and was suffering back pain due to such permanent physical disability.
Under the circumstances, the compensation awarded on the head of pain and sufferings is on the lower side.

For each fracture,
compensation of Rs.25,000/- should have been awarded, which comes to Rs.75,000/-.

Priyadarshini G.K vs Sathish on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83650990/
3 12.
The compensation on the head of loss of income during laid up period is based on the evidence.
The appellant herself deposes that she could not attend to job for 42 days.
The Tribunal has taken two months income as loss of income during laid up period.
The compensation awarded on the medical expenses is also based on the evidence adduced and the bills produced.
Therefore compensation awarded on those two heads do not call for any interference.
13. The Tribunal has awarded Rs.10,000/- as attendant charges.
The evidence on record shows that atleast for two months the appellant needed attendant.
Therefore the attendant charges at the rate of Rs.300/- per day shall have to be paid for two months, that comes to Rs.18,000/-.
14. So far as loss of amenities, the evidence discussed above shows that the appellant had compressed fracture of D5 and D8 and stable burst fracture and deformity of D6.
At the time of the accident, she was hardly 26 years.
She suffered difficulty in long sitting and she cannot take up heavy tasks.
Having regard to the disability suffered by her, compensation of Rs.25,000/- awarded on the head of loss of amenities is on the lower side.
The Tribunal ought to have awarded Rs.1,00,000/- on that head.

Hence, just compensation payable is as follows:
 Sl. Particulars Compensation  No. awarded in Rs.
 1. Pain and sufferings 75,000/-
 2. Loss of income during laid 61,600/-
 up period  3.

Medical expenses 86,766/-
 4. Attendant charges 18,000/-
 5. Loss of amenities 1,00,000/-

rounded of to  3,41,400/-
The order of the Tribunal needs to be modified accordingly.
The appeal deserves to be allowed in part.

Hence the following:
ORDER
The appeal is partly allowed.
The impugned award is modified as follows:
(i) The appellant/claimant is entitled to compensation of Rs.3,41,400/- with interest thereon at 8% per annum from the date of the petition till its realization.
(ii) Respondent No.2 shall deposit the said amount before the Tribunal within four weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this award.
On such deposit, the Tribunal shall release the amount to the appellant.
